lines.text: Folks, repentance is never walked alone. You have a friend. His name is El Shaddai. His name is Yahweh. And he will not give up on you until he has brought you safely home.
So, what are we supposed to do when we've walked the road of compromise? Like Naomi, we are to go home. We are to shuv, if you will. We are to walk that road of repentance.
What a glorious reality! God takes the marginalized, sin-city Moabite woman and based upon her personal risky faith, God exalts her as his cherished daughter. He does no less for us.

If you remember last week, it is not so much to stress that as it is to stress something of God's own heart simply to see Naomi come home. That is the longing that we should be carrying as we are reading through this. Naomi, just go home.

And so, it is simply to say that repentance is not so much about perfection as it is about direction, a process, a true journey home, and a messy one at that, where we are still taking steps in the right direction, but not necessarily where all the intricacies of our hearts and minds are content and settled in the Lord.

And so it is true here. This same word, shuv, is being used. And yes, for Naomi, it refers to one geographic place now to another that she is going, but it is the genius of the author to show that she is not just returning to Bethlehem as it is, she is returning to God.
